question: Should OpenClaw core support native cross-gateway session messaging now, and if so should it proceed through the narrow `gateway.peers` session-tool PR or wait for the broader Gateway federation contract?
rationale: This crosses Gateway trust, session-state, message-delivery, and credential boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API or security model.

options.title: Design Federation Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open and align the implementation with gateway identity, scopes, replay/idempotency, transcript ownership, and upgrade behavior before merging code.

options.title: Advance Narrow PR With Gates
options.body: Use the linked PR only after conflicts, real multi-gateway proof, security review, and compatibility behavior are resolved.

options.title: Defer Core Support
options.body: Document plugin/MCP/channel workarounds and close or downgrade native core support only if maintainers explicitly reject cross-gateway session routing for now.

recommendation.title: Design Federation Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and align the implementation with gateway identity, scopes, replay/idempotency, transcript ownership, and upgrade behavior before merging code.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the session-tool routing and security-scoping surface is Peter Steinberger's merged work in that path.
